Incidence and force of blood-stage infection, by origin

Source: R/metrics.R
force_of_infection.Rd

The cases of each window of the run, by origin, as counts (n, the incidence) and per host-year (rate). Among the new clones, imported + local reinfection give the mosquito-borne force of infection (FOI); adding relapse gives the molecular force of blood-stage infection (molFOB) – a compound measure that is elevated in P. vivax because relapses contribute new blood-stage clones (Koepfli et al. 2013). With detected_only = TRUE only the cases the observation layer reported are counted: the incidence, FOI and molFOB of a line list. Relapses are split into relapse (imported) and relapse (local) – a relapse of an imported genotype is a distinct truth category. Set split_imported = FALSE for a single relapse class. Either way origin comes back as a factor with all levels present, so the shape of the result depends on the argument and never on what the run happened to contain: pooling a grid cannot split one quantity across three columns.

Usage

force_of_infection(
  run,
  bin = 30,
  split_imported = TRUE,
  exclude_masked = FALSE,
  detected_only = FALSE
)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

bin

window width in days.

split_imported

split relapses by the provenance of the genotype. TRUE (default) gives five origin levels, FALSE gives four.

exclude_masked

if TRUE, leave out the masked relapses, into a patent clone of their own lineage (see classify_cases()): molFOB as a genotyping study measures it.

detected_only

if TRUE, count only the reported cases (detected == 1). Detection is drawn once per bite, import, activation or recrudescence (P_DETECT_PRIMARY, P_DETECT_RELAPSE, P_DETECT_RECRUD).

Value

a data.table with one row for every window of the run and every origin, by window: win (the window's first day, an integer: 0, bin, 2 * bin, ...), origin, n (the cases, clone onsets as rows of classify_cases(), 0 where there are none; episodes() groups them by host and day), days (the days the window covers within the run, which is SIM_DAYS days long whether or not it went extinct: bin - 1 for the first window, which starts on day 1, and fewer for the last when the run ends inside it), rate (per host-year, scaled by days) and is_acquisition. Sum only the is_acquisition rows for FOI or molFOB: a recrudescence is returned as its own row so incidence stays complete, but it is not a newly acquired clone.

Details

A recrudescence is returned as its own origin with is_acquisition = FALSE. It is a new patent episode but not a new clone, so including it would inflate molFOB – which counts clone acquisitions. Worth noting that a real molFOB, measured by comparing genotypes between study visits, would often count a recrudescence as a new clone, because the clone was undetectable at the previous visit; the gap between the two sums here estimates that bias.

References

Koepfli C, et al. (2013) A high force of Plasmodium vivax blood-stage infection drives the rapid acquisition of immunity in Papua New Guinean children. PLoS Negl Trop Dis 7(9):e2403.

See also

plot_force_of_infection()

force_of_infection(example_run(), bin = 100)
